plain_text:
Blood clots are a natural and necessary
part of healing, but they can sometimes
cause serious problems.
semantic_text: Blood clots are a natural and necessary part of healing, but they can sometimes cause serious problems.

plain_text:
Blood clots are made of proteins, platelets, and other cells in the
blood that thicken and stick together. When you cut yourself,
a blood clot forms over the injury. This stops the bleeding
and helps the wound to heal. Once the injury heals, your body
usually dissolves the clot.
semantic_text: Blood clots are made of proteins, platelets, and other cells in the blood that thicken and stick together. When you cut yourself, a blood clot forms over the injury. This stops the bleeding and helps the wound to heal. Once the injury heals, your body usually dissolves the clot.

plain_text:
Blood clots can also form inside the body when blood vessels
are injured or damaged. These clots can block blood flow to
important organs like the heart, brain, and lungs, which can
cause serious health problems.
semantic_text: Blood clots can also form inside the body when blood vessels are injured or damaged. These clots can block blood flow to important organs like the heart, brain, and lungs, which can cause serious health problems.

plain_text:
Watch this video from MedlinePlus to learn more
about how blood clots form.
semantic_text: Watch this video from MedlinePlus to learn more about how blood clots form.

plain_text:
Blood clots can form in your body's blood vessels, which are
part of your body's circulatory system.
semantic_text: Blood clots can form in your body's blood vessels, which are part of your body's circulatory system.

plain_text:
Clots that develop deep in our blood vessels can break off and
travel to other parts of the body. While these clots can form
anywhere in the body, they most commonly occur in the arms
and legs.
semantic_text: Clots that develop deep in our blood vessels can break off and travel to other parts of the body. While these clots can form anywhere in the body, they most commonly occur in the arms and legs.

plain_text:
Deep vein thrombosis is a blood clot that forms in a vein deep
in the body. It can break loose and cause a serious problem in
the lungs, called a pulmonary embolism.
semantic_text: Deep vein thrombosis is a blood clot that forms in a vein deep in the body. It can break loose and cause a serious problem in the lungs, called a pulmonary embolism.

plain_text:
Pulmonary embolism is a clot within the lungs that blocks
blood flow to areas of the lung, sometimes making it difficult
to breathe. Pulmonary embolism is a very dangerous condition.
It can damage the lungs and other organs in the body and even
cause death.
semantic_text: Pulmonary embolism is a clot within the lungs that blocks blood flow to areas of the lung, sometimes making it difficult to breathe. Pulmonary embolism is a very dangerous condition. It can damage the lungs and other organs in the body and even cause death.

plain_text:
Learn more about symptoms, causes, and treatments for deep
vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
semantic_text: Learn more about symptoms, causes, and treatments for deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.

plain_text:
■ There is damage to the lining of blood vessels. The damage
may be caused by an acute injury, surgery and other medical
procedures, or other health conditions that cause chronic
inflammation.
semantic_text: ■ There is damage to the lining of blood vessels. The damage may be caused by an acute injury, surgery and other medical procedures, or other health conditions that cause chronic inflammation.

plain_text:
■ Blood flow is sluggish or slow. Lack of motion can cause
sluggish or slow blood flow. This may occur after surgery, if
you're ill and in bed for a long time, or during extended travel.
■ Your blood is thicker or more likely to clot than normal.
Certain conditions can increase blood's tendency to clot.
So can some medical treatments such as chemotherapy
(which treats cancer) or birth control pills.
Often, blood clots form without any clear cause.
semantic_text: ■ Blood flow is sluggish or slow. Lack of motion can cause sluggish or slow blood flow. This may occur after surgery, if you're ill and in bed for a long time, or during extended travel. ■ Your blood is thicker or more likely to clot than normal. Certain conditions can increase blood's tendency to clot. So can some medical treatments such as chemotherapy (which treats cancer) or birth control pills. Often, blood clots form without any clear cause.

plain_text:
Blood clot symptoms will vary based on where the clot is located.


Many symptoms of blood clots are the same as symptoms of
other conditions. You can also have a clot and not experience any
noticeable symptoms.
semantic_text:
Blood clot symptoms will vary based on where the clot is located.

Many symptoms of blood clots are the same as symptoms of other conditions. You can also have a clot and not experience any noticeable symptoms.

plain_text:
In an arm or leg. If you have a clot in your arms or legs, it could
be a deep vein thrombosis. You might experience:
semantic_text: In an arm or leg. If you have a clot in your arms or legs, it could be a deep vein thrombosis. You might experience:

plain_text:
■ Pain (either sudden or gradual)
■ Swelling
■ Tenderness (hurts when touched)
■ Warmth or redness
semantic_text: ■ Pain (either sudden or gradual) ■ Swelling ■ Tenderness (hurts when touched) ■ Warmth or redness

plain_text:
In the lungs. A clot in the lungs (pulmonary embolism) can
cause symptoms such as:
semantic_text: In the lungs. A clot in the lungs (pulmonary embolism) can cause symptoms such as:

plain_text:
■ Shortness of breath
■ Chest pain (especially with deep breathing)
■ Sweating or a fever
■ Coughing up blood
semantic_text: ■ Shortness of breath ■ Chest pain (especially with deep breathing) ■ Sweating or a fever ■ Coughing up blood

plain_text:
In the abdomen. Blood clots can also form in the blood vessels
inside the abdomen. They can cause severe abdominal pain and
digestive issues (such as nausea and vomiting).
semantic_text: In the abdomen. Blood clots can also form in the blood vessels inside the abdomen. They can cause severe abdominal pain and digestive issues (such as nausea and vomiting).
